messages:
oliver: Heads up — multiple enterprise customers opened tickets about p99 token latency spikes starting ~03:00 UTC. Endpoint /v1/generate, model variant: gpt-open-16k-flashopt. p95 from ~220ms -> ~1.1s, p99 from ~480ms -> ~3.7s. Attaching a quick sample trace and a stack of logs. @maria @anita

maria: thanks. Can you paste a trace and whether these were cold or warm cache requests? any recent deploys? :eyes:

oliver: trace: request_id=abcd-1234, seq_len=2048, batch=1, kv_hits=partial. These are warm (many keys in cache). We had a runtime deploy around 02:45 UTC that included new compile flags for the FlashAttention kernel (kevin's change). Ticket IDs: T-4521, T-4523.

kevin: I landed a compile flag tweak (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runner/pull/672) to enable aggressive fma-tuning on flash kernel for Ampere. Rollout started 02:50 canary, 03:10 prod. I didn't see perf regressions in microbenchmarks but not with long-seq warm-cache profile.

anita: ok that matches timing. I'm running a quick internal smoke with seq=2048 to repro. Command I'm using: ```bash
python infra/tools/load_profile.py --model gpt-open-16k-flashopt --seq 2048 --batch 1 --tokens 512 --rps 5
```

anita: local reproducer shows p99 token latency jump after the compile flag enabled. When I toggle the kernel selection to fallback to SDPA (software fallback) p99 drops back to baseline.

maria: good repro. Can we roll a hotfix knob to revert that compile flag or enable kernel fallback heuristic for long sequences? We should also throttle canary to stop impact.

kevin: I can push a rollback patch to disable the new flag and add a heuristic to prefer SDPA for seq_len >= 1536 for now. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runner/pull/679 (WIP).

oliver: customers want ETA. Can we do a targeted rollback to Dedicated cluster only? Some customers on hosted still fine but several on dedicated complaining.

maria: yes — we can do a region/tier-scoped rollback. Anita, can you prepare a canary toggler config? We'll push to s1-dedicated first.

anita: prepared canary toggle: ``configs/runtime/kernel_toggle.yaml`` with knob: ``flashopt_compile=false`` for s1-dedicated canary, 10% hosts. I'll trigger after approval.

kevin: I'm going to attach a debug log snippet that shows kernel selection and compile path: ```
[2026-03-17T03:12:07Z] model=gpt-open-16k-flashopt seq=2048 kernel=flashopt compile_flags=FMA_TUNE aggressive status=compiled time_ms=3890
[2026-03-17T03:12:07Z] model=gpt-open-16k-sdpa seq=2048 kernel=sdpa compile_flags=default time_ms=420
```

maria: rough numbers — flashopt compiled path is 3.9s, sdpa path 0.42s for same seq on same hw. That suggests our aggressive tuning hits a bad kernel path for long sequences. Likely cache/KV interplay.

anita: rolling the canary now to s1-dedicated 10% -> monitor: deploy-bot: "canary toggle deploy started by anita at 03:40 UTC"

deploy-bot: "deploy finished: canary flashopt_compile=false on s1-dedicated (10%) — id=deploy-8903"

anita: initial telemetry looks good — p99 on canary hosts back to baseline (p99 ~450ms). Will increase to 30% in 10m if stable. :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll hold the PR and add an automated kernel-selection heuristic: if seq_len >= 1536 or kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.7 then prefer sdpa. That should avoid future regressions while we debug the aggressive FMA tuning.

maria: also add a monitoring alert rule to catch flash kernel p95/p99 divergence vs sdpa (threshold: 2x baseline for 5m). Link the rule to the runbook.

oliver: relaying to customers: initial fix is toggling compile flag for dedicated clusters — ETA full rollback 45m, incremental updates as canary proves stable.

anita: scaling canary to 30% now. deploy-bot: "scaling canary to 30% — deploy-8903"

deploy-bot: "canary scaled: 30% complete"

anita: metrics stable at 30% for 15m. escalating to 100% for dedicated tier now.

deploy-bot: "rolling to 100% s1-dedicated — job deploy-8903"

sre-oncall: monitoring dashboards show p99 returning to baseline on all dedicated hosts. I'll keep an eye for 30m and follow up with incident summary.

maria: follow-up actions: 1) keep flag disabled for 48h on dedicated, 2) merge kevin's heuristic before re-enabling aggressive tuning, 3) create regression test with long-seq warm-cache profile in CI, 4) postmortem note.

kevin: agreed. I'll add the heuristic + unit test and ping for an ops roll next week.

oliver: closing customer escalations with update and offering credits for affected windows. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

maria: filing short postmortem and linking PRs and the runbook. Will add repro steps and the exact load_profile command we used.

anita: leaving a quick snippet for repro in the runbook: ```bash
# reproduce p99 regression locally
python infra/tools/load_profile.py --model gpt-open-16k-flashopt --seq 2048 --batch 1 --tokens 512 --rps 5 --warm-cache
# toggle knob locally:
redctl runtime set kernel_toggle.flashopt_compile false
```

maria: thanks — marking this thread resolved unless new noise appears.

oliver: noted, closing ticket after 2h monitoring window. :white_check_mark:
